subtitle: A 22.5-kilometer barrier island resort strip that Mexico's central bank picked by computer in 1969, built from an uninhabited mangrove island into Quintana Roo's tourism engine.
spike_statement: In 1969 a Bank of Mexico trust scored coastlines by computer and picked this mangrove island, population three, to become Cancún.

levers.photo_tone: Turquoise Caribbean shallows against a wall of glass hotel towers on Boulevard Kukulcán, the barrier island's narrow spine pinched between open sea and lagoon haze
